scope: Classification of unchanged strict manual-pronunciation failures. This does not rewrite gold, turn a regression into held-out evidence, or equate all uses of IPA ɐ and ə.

ukSource.license: Retained UK lexical records remain GPL-3.0-only; see ipa-dict/GPL-3.0.txt. Classification prose is PageNarrator GPL-3.0-or-later.
ukSource.accentLabel: The source labels en_UK as Received Pronunciation; its fixed citation-form IPA records were generated via ipacards/eSpeak, not a human recording of these words.

interpretation: Phonetician Geoff Lindsey's original discussion and recorded examples document a lowered word-final COMMA vowel, including ɐ, within British accent variation. Each difference below is confined to the final unstressed citation vowel; stress and the preceding segment sequence are otherwise one of the original manual alternatives. These are source-faithful final-vowel variants, not lookup/converter corruption. A fixed isolated-word variant cannot establish ideal connected-speech allophony or guarantee a neural model's exact acoustic realization.

separateContextualV2Observation.interpretation: The US unstressed prefix ə is a retained legitimate verb variant alongside ɪ (record(3)); the v2 manual verb gold initially listed only ɪ. That narrow-vowel discrepancy does not excuse the real noun/verb stress-selection failures exposed by v2. Original v2 gold and first failure report remain unchanged.
